  doing                                                                       
  it by hand five more times is how the fleet ends up with five subtly        
  different                                                                   
  boxes and nobody able to say which.                                         
                                                                              
   deploy/mesh-node.service  exists and is the only part that is written down.
                                                                              
  ## What to build                                                            
                                                                              
  One command that takes a node from bare Ubuntu to running, and is safe to   
  run                                                                         
  twice. Re-running must converge, not duplicate — that is the same property  
   node.reconcile  has and for the same reason: the thing you reach for when  
  something looks wrong has to be safe to reach for.                          
                                                                              
  It must handle:                                                             
                                                                              
  • Node 22 and git, if absent                                                
  • a clone (or a pull to a pinned ref) into  /srv/mesh-serve                 
  •  npm install  and  npm run build  on the box — verified to work in        
  981MB, but that is the tightest machine in the fleet and the margin is thin 
  •  /etc/mesh/node.env , mode 600, never with secrets on a command line —    
  an argument is visible in  ps  to every user on the box.  surf  was done by 
  piping the file over stdin; that pattern works and is worth keeping.        
  • the systemd unit from  deploy/ , enabled                                  
  • a verification step that says plainly whether the node came up, rather    
  than                                                                        
  exiting 0 because  systemctl enable  succeeded

  Do not put  MESH_KEY  or  MONGODB_URI  in the repository, in a default, or

  script

  placeholder                                                                 
  ends up committed.

  mesh port; every other node binds loopback and dials out. FLYBYME/surfdns#50

Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>

    The startup banner does not print the database password
    
    It wrote the mongo URI verbatim. Against mongodb://localhost:27017 that is
    harmless and it is what every local run shows, so it survived. The first time a
    node was pointed at Atlas it printed a live mongodb+srv://user:password@... into
    the systemd journal -- on every boot, readable by anything that can read
    journals, and shipped wherever logs get shipped. The credential is now burned.
    
    A banner exists to say where am I pointed, which the host and database name
    answer completely. The credential was never part of the question.
    
    Also prints the host it actually binds rather than a hardcoded 127.0.0.1: on the
    head that is 0.0.0.0, and printing loopback made a node reachable from the
    internet look like one that was not. See surfdns#50 -- WSTransport ignores the
    host argument entirely, so the banner was wrong in the safe direction while the
    socket was wrong in the dangerous one.
    
    Adds deploy/mesh-node.service: the systemd unit for a node, with secrets in an
    EnvironmentFile rather than the command line, because an argument is visible in
    ps to every user on the box.

diff --git a/deploy/mesh-node.service b/deploy/mesh-node.service
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ba526cf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/deploy/mesh-node.service
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+[Unit]
+Description=mesh-serve node
+Documentation=https://github.com/FLYBYME/mesh-serve
+After=network-online.target
+Wants=network-online.target
+
+[Service]
+Type=simple
+WorkingDirectory=/srv/mesh-serve
+
+# Secrets and per-machine values live here, not in this unit and not in the
+# command line: an argument is visible in `ps` to every user on the box.
+#   MESH_KEY       the shared key a peer presents at the WebSocket handshake
+#   MONGODB_URI    Atlas, so cluster state lives on no single node
+#   CDN_PORT/URL   what this node advertises to peers for blob fetches
+EnvironmentFile=/etc/mesh/node.env
+
+# --ws-host 0.0.0.0 only on the head. Every other node binds 127.0.0.1 and dials
+# out to it, so exactly one machine has a port on the internet.
+ExecStart=/usr/bin/node bin/node.mjs --ws 4001 --ws-host 0.0.0.0 --cdn 8080 --api 5005 --db mesh-serve-live
+
+# systemd owns the process; the Supervisor owns services inside it. Two
+# supervisors, one boundary: `node.assign` starts and stops services live and
+# must never need a restart, or systemd's restart policy and the fleet's desired
+# state become two authorities over one thing.
+Restart=always
+RestartSec=5
+
+# surf has 981MB of RAM and is the tightest box in the fleet. A node that dies of
+# OOM and is restarted by systemd is recoverable; one that takes the box down
+# with it is a drive to a datacentre.
+MemoryMax=600M
+OOMPolicy=stop
+
+StandardOutput=journal
+StandardError=journal
+SyslogIdentifier=mesh-node
+
+[Install]
+WantedBy=multi-user.target
